# The observable container spec, regenerated by an agent in two bindings

Leonardo Rossi wrote the design of his observable containers, item models and row selection down as a
specification an AI agent can regenerate the library from: [`SPEC.md` and `PROMPT.md`](https://gist.github.com/96Ven96/100c0ec4917dced4d6c8ac9a4cc06b7e)
(revision `d1e540d`). He offered it as a contribution and asked to be told where an agent trips.
This directory is the answer. The gist carries no license, so its text is credited and linked here, not copied.

| | Binding A | Binding B |
|---|---|---|
| Signals | two non-template `QObject` classes through classic moc, keys as `QVariant` | typed signals declared in the class templates through reflect-moc, no moc input |
| Language | C++20 | C++26 with `-freflection` (GCC 16.2) |
| Directory | [`binding_a`](binding_a) | [`binding_b`](binding_b) |
| Build | standalone: `cmake -S binding_a -B build` | standalone, or through `tests/qt` of this repository |
| Acceptance tests (ctest) | 17 of 17 | 17 of 17 |

## How it was made

Two agents, each started fresh with no other code in view, each given the generation prompt and the spec
(binding A: `SPEC.md` and `PROMPT.md` only; binding B: the same two files and the reflect-moc headers, with the
observable models of this repository removed from its copy). Neither could run git or reach credentials.
Each was asked to write down every ambiguity and every acceptance test result.

Hand changes after generation, all in `binding_b/CMakeLists.txt`: the default reflect-moc include directory
points at this repository, `reflect_moc_qt` is not defined twice when the directory is added as a subdirectory,
and the compile-fail tests take the `rqt_build_tree` lock the other tests of `tests/qt` use. Nothing else was edited.

Both trees were rebuilt by hand from a read-only mount before they were committed: 0 warnings at
`-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`, all 17 ctest entries pass (acceptance tests AT-1.1 to AT-9.6, the six compile-fail
twin and break pairs included). Binding A also builds with MSVC 19.44 and Qt 6.8.3 at `/W4 /permissive- /Zc:__cplusplus`
with 0 warnings and the same 17 of 17 (CI job `spec-binding-a-msvc`).

Not done: Clang for binding B (it needs reflection, which only GCC 16 has here), binding B on MSVC, queued
connections and threads, QML, key types other than `int`, `quint32`, `qsizetype` and `QString`. The generated code is pinned by the
acceptance tests and is not held to the CRAP and mutation rules of the hand-written examples; the binding B agent
ran five hand-made mutants and one survived, which it killed with a new test (`at_3_6_replaceWritesBetweenTheAboutAndTheTwin`).

## Where the spec needed a decision

Fifteen points in binding A. The reading each agent chose is the one that changes nothing and emits nothing
when the spec is silent (its rule R2).

1. 6.2: `is_std_array_v` strips cv-ref itself; the text does not say who does.
2. 9.4: the order of "last occurrence wins" and "skip unchanged" is not given. Deduplicate first, then drop unchanged cells. The other order writes a stale value for `[(c, new), (c, current)]`.
3. 9.2: "empty" for the matrix `clear()` means no rows and no columns.
4. 9.1 and 9.3: NaN written over a NaN cell when the sentinel is not NaN counts as a change.
5. 8.1: `HashableKey` is stated only in the associative paragraph; a `static_assert` in the class, no `requires` (15.4 lists only `SupportedContainer`).
6. 8.2: `entryDataChanged` for a key with no row emits nothing.
7. 7.2: the key order of `insertMany` follows the iteration order of `entries`, which is arbitrary for `QHash`.
8. 7.2: batch keys are deduplicated in O(n) when hashable, O(n²) otherwise.
9. 10.2: the cost of the Multi `hasSelection()` and `count()` is not given; a private counter makes both O(1).
10. 10.5: `selectedValue` on a Multi tracker gives one message, from a `static_assert` in both overloads.
11. 10.5: the Single `applySelectionValue` early returns are one test, `isSelected(row) == requested`.
12. 11 T13 against 12.8 AT-8.4: T13 removes row 2, AT-8.4 says to apply it to the new selected row (3). Row 3 was used.
13. 14 against 15.2 and 15.5: `src/obs_signals.cpp` may include only the two headers while the synopsis declares only constructors, so the constructors are inline in the headers.
14. 12: `QSignalSpy` for counts was not needed; the recorders give order and counts.
15. 12.4: the test model "implements `roleNames`" while the base class has one; it calls the base and adds a role.

Binding B added: no constructors for the example models (10.7, so they start empty and tests fill them with
`resetWith`); `onStructureChanged` and `onKeysAdded` take any source type and pass typed keys (7.3 and 15.2 name
`ContainerSignals`, which binding B does not have); a non-const `Container*` would select the reference overload of
`selectedValue`, so that overload excludes pointers.

## Where the spec looks wrong

1. 8.3: batch removal calls `beginRemoveRows` after the container has erased the entries, so `data()` of the doomed rows is invalid during the cycle. A proxy or view that reads them in `rowsAboutToBeRemoved` sees nothing. The spec chose this on purpose (C5); it is a trade-off.
2. 7.1 against G3: G3 lists "a value already equal" as nothing changed, but `replace` always notifies.
3. 14 against 6.4 and 10.5: `sel_kit` is meant to be independent of `obs_kit`, but the Multi `clearSelectionAndNotify` needs `contiguousRuns`, which section 6.4 puts in `obs`. Both agents included `obs/traits.h`.
4. 15.3: `template <class Self = C>` lets a caller write `insertMany<QHash<int, int>>(...)` on a `QList` container and defeat the `static_assert`.
5. 10.6: `rowInserted` returns nothing, so every host compares `selectedRow()` before and after; returning a `Delta` as `rowRemoved` does would remove that.
6. 10.2 and 10.7: a Multi tracker starts with 0 rows and the example models have no constructor, so a host over existing rows must call `reset(n)` first or the `Q_ASSERT` fires.
7. 16: the Qt API list is smaller than the spec needs (`QModelIndex`, `Qt::ItemFlags`, `Qt::Orientation`, `CheckIndexOption`, `QObject::disconnect`, `QMetaObject::Connection`, and in the tests `QVariant::toString`, `toInt`, `toDouble`, `QString::number`, `QChar`).
8. Binding B only: 6.1 `VariantKey` and AT-1.8 test a requirement 4.2 drops, 15.2 takes `const ContainerSignals *`, 14 lists an AUTOMOC `obs_kit`, and the spec says C++20 throughout while reflect-moc needs C++26. A short table of the binding B readings of section 15 would save the translation.

## Binding A on MSVC and Clang: one thing to watch

In `Container<QList<T>>`, `insert(qsizetype, Value)` and `insert(const Key &, Value)` have the same signature and
differ only in their `requires` clause. GCC 16.2, MSVC 19.44 and Clang 19.1.7 all accept it. The Clang run was by
hand, in the image with Debian's `clang` package against Qt 6.10.3 (`-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++`): 17 of 17, no
warning at `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`, and the compile-fail pairs match their expected text. There is no CI job for it.

## Binding B and reflect-moc

- `#include <QtTest/QtTest>` fails under `-std=c++26` with this Qt 6.10.3 and libstdc++ (`'saturate_cast' has not been declared in 'std'` in `q26numeric.h`); the per-class QtTest headers work.
- QtTest runs only private no-argument slots, so every test function carries `[[= rqt::slot]]`. An unannotated one is skipped without a message; the agent compared the executable totals with the number of annotated functions.
- `RQT_OBJECT` must come first in the class.

## Repeat it

```sh
# binding A, any compiler with Qt 6
cmake -S examples/qt/spec_regen/binding_a -B build-a && cmake --build build-a && ctest --test-dir build-a

# both bindings and the repository, in the image
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/src -w /src reflect-moc/gcc16-qt610 \
  sh -c 'cmake --preset qt && cmake --build --preset qt -j"$(nproc)" && ctest --preset qt -j2'

# the comparison, gate first
docker run --rm -e RQT_RUNS=7 -v "$PWD":/src:ro -w /src reflect-moc/gcc16-qt610 bash tests/qt/measure/spec_bench/run.sh
```

The numbers are in [`docs/measurements.md`](../../../docs/measurements.md).
